timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Welcome to WISIS Forum 2019. This year we celebrate the 10-year anniversary of what has become
the world's largest ICT for good community event and I am especially delighted to join the
new chairman of the forum this year, Mr. Mustafa Jabba. He is a minister for the post telecommunications
and Information Technology of Bangladesh. Thank you very much for joining us.
Thank you very much also. Mr. Jabba, how do you use ICT in Bangladesh to help deliver
the sustainable development goals? You have already mentioned that I am from Bangladesh.
You will realize that Bangladesh is a very young country in South Asia with a history of
only 40-80 years. We have to have a bloody war and the major and significant thing was that
Bangladesh is a agro-based country. We have not joined the first, second or third industrial
revolution and suddenly we realize that fourth industrial revolution is here. So it has become
a very challenging thing to transform a country from agro-based to a digital country and you'll
be happy to know that we are the first country in the world who has declared digital Bangladesh and
from 2009 onwards this is also 10-year of our prime minister's office and she has transformed
the country to a digital one. What we realize is that the world is not flat, it is not a plain land
and the countries around the world are not of same circumstances. So there are countries who are
industrialized, heavily industrialized and there are countries like Bangladesh. So the technologies
which are coming now including 5G, artificial intelligence, robotics and all other things,
these are all disruptive technologies and it is an opportunity, it is also a challenging thing.
So the world will have to accommodate the new technologies in its own way, every country will
have to be very serious about the challenges and the problems like I can give you an example.
Say we are looking at a drive-all-eska so that we will eliminate 1.2 billion jobs. So somebody
will have to be happy that we do not have people and if the car is driven automatically then I
do not need a man. But someone like Bangladesh will have to think that I have people but they will do
those who are not digital skill. So these differences will be there and these challenges will be there.
So WSIES is definitely a good platform for the transformation because I remember it started,
it is first declaration in Chennai in 2003 and the vision was to have an information society.
To be very frank it was really not known to the whole world what is an information society
and what they were talking about. When somebody was talking about a knowledge-based economy
people were thinking what is that, what it looks like that and where are the workers.
In fact thanks to WSIES that they have started the whole proposition and in fact they have formed
a forum, the WSIES forum and that forum has crossed 10th year and this is definitely a
significant achievement for the whole world. The important thing for WSIES, I remember is that
they are addressing the whole world not the industrialized countries alone or the rich economies.
They are trying to penetrate through every corner of the world that's very inclusive idea
because if you cannot include everybody of the world in the new technologies of the new
civilization it will be very difficult to implement because the world is in such a way that
it is diversified. So we have to accommodate that diversification also address the poorest
country and the rich access to both. WSIES is playing a very important role in organizing these
things. This forum is working very hard and keeping everybody on the platform and I wish that this
is a good opportunity for everybody. I am really happy because a man from Bangladesh has become
the chairman of WSIES forum summit. This is something very big for me. It is a great honor and I am
really grateful to the WSIES forum particularly the secretary general and howl and jow is very
serious and friendly person. I have met him twice before and I found him very friendly.
You have touched upon a very important aspect of WSIES forum and its collaboration.
We will only create a fair and equal information society through collaboration.
That is the whole thing that we have to think of it. In fact when we were in the
gradient society the people were isolated. They were working in their fields and they were
just thinking of their villages or our surroundings. But today's world is not an isolated island.
The world is connected to each other. Every people is connected to in fact each other with the
advent of the new technologies like 5G, the speed of internet, the advent of new technologies.
I think the whole scenario is going to be something like that everybody has to participate in the
activities of the world to go forward. So you cannot leave anyone alone or any country out of
this platform. So this collaboration is important and one of the most important thing I must mention
here is that WSIES was the first organization who was talking about information society.
We have to understand that today's world is a different world. It mentions that information
is the assets, information is the wealth. So information is not limited to reach countries.
Information is with the poorest countries or a young boy. Information can be with the country
who has not even heard about WSIES. But one of the major things which WSIES connecting is also the
innovation innovation of the young people, the activities of the small and medium enterprises
and also connecting the oven forces. I think this is something which is a collaborative world and
definitely this is going to deliver a knowledge-based society. I am hoping for that.
Mr. Mustafa Jada the new chairman of WSIES Forum. Thank you very much.
Thank you very much again and my best wishes to all the participants of this forum.
